sn12.23:1.2: The “ending of defilements” (_āsavānaṁ khayaṁ_) is a common sutta term for arahantship. | “Knowing and seeing” refers to the penetrating insight that arises from meditative immersion (_samādhi_, eg. [an5.168:2.2](), [an10.2:2.3](), [sn12.23:6.18](), [dn2:83.1]()). | The opening is the same as [sn22.101]() and [sn22.101]().
sn12.23:2.1: An _upanisā_ is a conditional factor that is both necessary and strongly conducive. It functions as a contraction of _upanissaya_ (“depend on”). Elsewhere, _saupanisa_ is used of the seven path factors as “vital conditions” for right immersion ([sn45.28:1.2](), [mn117:2.1]()). Pali _upanisā_ is also found in the distinct sense “sitting close” to a teacher ([an3.67:6.7]()). | It is not clear if _upanisā_ is the same as the Sanskrit _upaniṣad_, for which the oldest sense is “correspondence, equivalence”, referring to the secret links between things (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 10.4.5.1; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.9.26, 4.2.1; Chāndogya Upaniṣad 3.11.3, 8.8.4; Taittirīya Upaniṣad 1.11.4, 2.9.1). These equivalences are explained in the esoteric teachings that themselves came to be known as Upaniṣads.
sn12.23:2.3: “Freedom” here is the liberation from defilements, namely arahantship itself. The arahant reviews their freedom, which is the “knowledge of ending”.
sn12.23:2.6: “Dispassion” (_virāga_) has a dual sense in Pali: a state where lust (_rāga_) is absent, and the process of defilements “fading away”, which leans on the sense of _rāga_ as “dye” (eg. the “fading away of ignorance” at [sn12.51:9.4]()).
sn12.23:2.9: “Disillusionment” (_nibbidā_) is the turning away in disappointment upon realizing that one cannot get what one wants ([mn50:31.15](), [sn35.240:1.8]()).
sn12.23:2.12: This is the insight of stream-entry.
sn12.23:2.15: “Immersion” (_samādhi_) general term for the absorptions (_jhāna_) and other profound meditations free of the hindrances. The mind in such a state is extremely bright and powerful. For a meditator with right view, their mind naturally inclines towards insight into the suffering of holding on and the bliss of letting go.
sn12.23:3.2: Immersion is a an integrated emotional state of heightened consciousness, and its primary condition is deep, pervasive, lasting, and subtle bliss or pleasure (_sukha_). It cannot be realized with purely neutral feeling.
sn12.23:3.5: “Tranquility” is a settled and serene body and mind, as activities or energies become stilled through the process of meditation.
sn12.23:3.8: “Rapture” (_pīti_) is a joyous emotional response to pleasure, manifesting as a spiritual sense of elevation or uplift in meditation.
